name: Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires nomination by an Australian state or territory government, which adds 5 points to the points test but also commits the applicant to living in that state/territory for a period.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for nomination through the relevant state/territory's own skilled migration program.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires an occupation on the MLTSSL or STSOL (Short-term Skilled Occupation List), plus a positive skills assessment.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain a positive skills assessment for a qualifying occupation.

value.note: 65-point minimum including the +5 state nomination bonus

requirements.blocker_text: This requires at least 65 points including the +5 points added by state nomination.

sources.title: Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) - Department of Home Affairs

notes: Broader occupation list than subclass 189 (STSOL as well as MLTSSL) and a real points advantage (+5), making this genuinely more accessible for many applicants than 189 — worth surfacing as the practical fallback when someone doesn't have a 189-eligible MLTSSL occupation or can't reach a competitive independent points score. Same permanent-on-grant structure as 189, same citizenship timeline logic. State nomination processes vary meaningfully by state/territory (each runs its own program with its own occupation priorities and sometimes its own points thresholds) — not modeled as separate requirement groups here given the number of jurisdictions involved, a real scope simplification flagged honestly.
